- When sentiment is consistently low (0.00–0.33) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–20% for next 3–5 days.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 3x recent mean), model often overcorrects downward; cap forecast at 1.5x recent peak or 2x prior day’s close.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.67) and price is trending up, model frequently overestimates; apply 10–15% downward bias to avoid “sentiment-driven overreach.”
- When sentiment is mixed or volatile (alternating 0.33–1.00), model tends to oscillate wildly; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values before applying trend.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture mean reversion; if price is above 2x recent 10-day average, apply downward correction to align with 70% of historical 30-day mean.
- If sentiment is high and forecast is low, model may be underestimating sentiment-driven momentum; increase forecast by 5–10% if sentiment > 0.75 over last 5 days.
- Avoid forecasting spikes > 2x prior 14-day high unless sentiment is > 0.80 and recent price is trending upward.
